title: The volatility risk premium: implied versus realized volatility
summary: Investors earn risk premiums for extra risk: equities over cash, credit over risk-free, long maturities over short. Option sellers earn the volatility risk premium: the gap between implied volatility and the realized volatility the stock actually delivers. That gap is the measuring stick for whether a stock is a good candidate for selling options.

steps.caption: A stock price path. Option sellers are paid to carry the risk of its moves.
Realized volatility measures how much the stock actually moved.
Implied volatility is what option prices assume the stock will move.
The volatility risk premium is implied minus realized. A wide, steady gap makes a better candidate for selling options.
When realized rises above implied, the premium turns negative and the seller loses.

takeaways: A risk premium is extra pay for taking extra risk, as with equities, credit and longer maturities.
The volatility risk premium is implied volatility minus realized volatility.
Use it to judge whether a stock is a good candidate for selling options.
caveats: The speaker mentions his own VAY metric and website; these are promotional and not verified.
